observations: Torah #190 cannot support any packages — new or existing — because the teaching contains zero bechina relationships. The algorithm requires at least 3 concepts forming an independent domain through shared-nature (bechina) connections. Torah #190 is a philosophical-legal analysis of Exodus 19 whose entire argument structure is eitza (cause-and-effect): God's direct speech eliminates free choice; God's speaking only to Moshe (not Israel) restores Israel's free choice; God commanding only two days (while Moshe independently adds a third) creates the space for Moshe's free choice. The key concepts — בחירה, דיבור, מוכרח, ישראל, משה, קבלת התורה — are linked by causal necessity, not by shared essential nature. A package formed from these concepts would violate the framework's core rule that packages are built on bechina edges only, not eitza chains. Recommendation: Torah #190 should be flagged in the dataset as an 'eitza-only' or 'analytical' Torah that contributes no bechina nodes to the graph. Its eitza relationships (divine speech → compulsion; indirect hearing → free choice; self-initiated action → free choice) could be added as eitza edges to enrich the causal flow graph, but no packages are appropriate at this time.
